prompt: Your phone case business brings in revenue of $3x^2 + 5x$ dollars and pays costs of $x^2 + 2x$ dollars. Write the profit: revenue minus cost.
hint: Profit is the money that comes in minus the money that goes out. Take care when subtracting a whole expression.

hints.text: Profit is the money that comes in minus the money that goes out. Take care when subtracting a whole expression.
Write $(3x^2 + 5x) - (x^2 + 2x)$ and distribute the minus to get $3x^2 + 5x - x^2 - 2x$. Combine the $x^2$-terms, then the $x$-terms.
$3x^2 - x^2 = 2x^2$ and $5x - 2x = 3x$, so the profit is $2x^2 + 3x$ dollars.

explanation: Profit is revenue minus cost, so write $(3x^2 + 5x) - (x^2 + 2x)$.
Distribute the minus sign to both cost terms so each one is subtracted: $3x^2 + 5x - x^2 - 2x$.
Combine like terms, matching squares with squares: $3x^2 - x^2 = 2x^2$ and $5x - 2x = 3x$.
Putting the two results together, the profit is $2x^2 + 3x$ dollars.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two sticker piles
steps: x²-terms are one kind of sticker, x-terms are another — never mix the piles.
x² pile: 3 minus 1 leaves 2, so 2x². x pile: 5 minus 2 leaves 3, so 3x.

alternativeExplanations.title: Try a sales number
steps: Say x = 10 cases. Revenue: 3(100) + 50 = 350 dollars. Cost: 100 + 20 = 120 dollars.
Profit: 350 − 120 = 230. Check the formula: 2(100) + 3(10) = 230. It works.
